purpose: Resolve whether HAILSTONE delay/surviving transport assets create extra Eniwetok garrison strength.
historical_anchors: 1st Amphibious Brigade was about 3,940 men on formation; only a portion physically reached Eniwetok, while other personnel/transports remained in the Truk/Ponape system.
Aikoku Maru attempted a Brown/Eniwetok-area reinforcement run in early Feb 1944 but aborted under US air pressure and later returned toward Truk.
Historical HAILSTONE destroyed Aikoku Maru at Truk; sources disagree on the exact passenger-unit identity/number aboard, so personnel accounting must remain banded.

reason: The early-Feb eastbound reinforcement corridor is already under US carrier/land-air pressure and is not reopened by a 3-day HAILSTONE delay.
After Kwajalein falls, moving a loaded transport east toward a soon-to-be-assaulted fixed island has lower expected value than preserving troops/ship westward.
Branch Truk evacuation doctrine explicitly removes mobile/high-value logistics assets before the raid.
centered_decision.destination: Ponape/Palau/Rabaul/western reserve pipeline; exact unit identity remains OPEN
centered_decision.future_effect: These survivors may strengthen later western garrisons but are not available to CATCHPOLE.

HAILSTONE_accounting_guard: Current Branch HAILSTONE shipping/death totals already excluded a historical Aikoku-style catastrophic transient-ship loss, so do not subtract the same people twice.
